criterion: every surface works end-to-end or fails with a named, user-visible state (unknown ≠ empty ≠ zero); no dead control
section: Binding definitions; W6; W14; W18; W19
message: W6 freezes a closed thirteen-member NamedState enum and a single render_state() primitive, and the binding text forbids waves from inventing trichotomy words. Later surface waves still invent user-facing states outside that set: W14 “named unavailable,” W18 “unsupported-preview,” W19 “unknown-preference.” A future maintainer must either (a) ship labels that bypass render_state (exactly the hand-invented labels the plan bans), or (b) silently overload unknown / cannot_* and collapse distinct failures. Either path re-creates dead or mislabelled empties on real controls. The enum, the binding allow-list, and every surface-local “named X state” must be one closed, amendable registry before surface waves run—not three competing vocabularies.

criterion: unknown ≠ empty ≠ zero; every health/usage/diagnose surface fails with a named, user-visible state
section: Binding definitions (Vocabulary bijection); W8; Hardening-gate failure-state table vocabulary
message: The plan requires STATE-VOCABULARY-MAP.md to be a machine-read bijection where “every term on both sides appears exactly once,” then immediately violates that math: empty-but-valid splits into empty, zero_measured, and pending; cannot_* is an open family; surface tables must also carry separate unknown/empty rows in surface-native language. A future maintainer implementing table_validator.py cannot satisfy “exactly once both ways” and the multi-map / open-set rules at the same time. The validator will be weakened, skipped, or green while mapping wrong—and wrong maps are how unknown becomes empty and zero becomes subscription. Replace “bijection / exactly once” with an explicit multi-map schema (dependency term → one or more NamedState + required surface rows) and make that the only thing the validator enforces.

criterion: Cost never fabricates dollars; dead control / silent zero / mislabelled empty / raw binary never exit via E6; nothing silent-claims the North Star
section: W2 Exit register; uses of E1–E6 across W1, W4, W8, W12, W21, W22
message: W2 builds a machine exit register around ExitId E1–E6 and hard rules (E2 illegal for dollars, E6 closed for the four North-Star violation classes, no exit-justified-by-exit), but the draft never defines what E1, E3, E4, or E5 mean as exits—only scattered uses (“no E5 on the task triple,” E4 reduced instrumentation, E3 out-of-criteria, E1 not-available, E2 provisional-with-as_of). A future maintainer cannot implement validate_justification, conjunction scoring, or S1 routing without inventing semantics. Invented semantics are how a silent-zero or fabricated-dollar finding gets an illegal exit and how the terminal status string lies. Require a binding EXIT-SEMANTICS table (id, legal criteria, required evidence shape, forbidden justifications, user-visible substitute) as a W2 deliverable, and make every later E-reference a row id in that table.

criterion: open/run/stop/restart + Doctor diagnose + session attach; every claiming surface honest; Steward proof only at S1
section: Success criteria; W2 terminal_status; W3 inventory scope; W21 TRACEABILITY-MATRIX
message: The plan speaks of “ten criteria,” “criteria 1–8 plus open and run,” and a matrix with “one row per criterion 1–10,” but nowhere lists the numbered ten with stable names. Success criteria are a bullet soup; W3’s control list is partial; W21’s matrix cannot be filled without invention. A future maintainer (or Foreman wave) will invent criterion numbers, omit attach or restart, or stamp CANDIDATE-MET on the wrong row—then S1 cannot convert structure to MET honestly. Add a binding numbered criteria table (1–10, North-Star phrase, owning wave(s), inventory controls) and make terminal_status, freeze NORTH-STAR CONTROL DECISION, and TRACEABILITY-MATRIX import that table by id only.

criterion: Nothing in this effort ships to v1.1.x collaborators; open/run/stop/restart and Doctor/attach on branch v1.2 without dead controls
section: W1 containment smoke; Success criteria Handoff; product deliverables under anchor/, tools/, tests/
message: W1 requires containment_smoke.py to assert “every write target resolves under planning/sleep-2026-07-28/stage2/” while nearly every later wave’s real deliverables are product paths (anchor/ui/…, anchor/session/…, anchor/doctor/…, tools/, tests/). Handoff only clarifies that the doc-trio lives under planning/ and “root foreign Foreman artifacts” stay untouched—it does not reconcile the absolute “every write under planning/” rule with shipping v1.2 product code. A future maintainer will either (a) put production code under planning/ (unshippable to the real app), (b) write into Anchor and fail containment forever, or (c) disable the smoke and lose the v1.1.x safety floor. Split write classes in the smoke: planning artifacts must stay under stage2; product tree writes are allow-listed under explicit Anchor paths; foreign Foreman root artifacts remain byte-identical—and name the allow-list as a signed ledger row.

criterion: unknown ≠ empty ≠ zero as separate user-visible states on every claiming surface
section: Binding definitions; W8 table_validator; Hardening-gate Failure-state table vocabulary; wave-local failure-states/*.md
message: Authors are told three incompatible table shapes at once: (1) five hardening dependency rows, (2) separate unknown and empty NamedState rows, (3) surface-native action language only, with index/rebuild banned on user tiles. W8 fails “honesty theater” and “missing required row,” but never shows one canonical filled table (columns, required keys, how empty-but-valid becomes two/three rows, where status code vs user text live). Future maintainers will copy the wrong shape; the validator will thrash; surfaces will green with merged unknown/empty. Ship one normative example table and a JSON/YAML schema the validator loads—prose checklists are not a schema.

criterion: open, run, stop, restart, Doctor diagnose, session attach all honest before North Star can be claimed
section: W10–W20 Depends-on graph; W21 surface-wave join gate
message: Most Phase-3 waves declare Depends-on: W9 only; W11/W17 depend on W10 for dead_control; W21 depends only on W20 but then asserts a join gate over W10–W20 GREEN. Future maintainer / Foreman topo-sort can start W12–W20 before W10’s shared dead-control primitive exists, or treat W21 as unblocked when only W20 is green while restart or Doctor is still OPEN—exactly when a dead-control audit mistakes “not built yet” for “clean.” Encode the real DAG: shared primitives (W6–W10) before importers; W21 Depends-on: W10–W20 (or an explicit join wave), not W20 alone; ban parallel GO on importers until dead_control and render_state commit SHAs exist.

criterion: surfaces work or fail named; cost never fabricates dollars (proof must be re-runnable)
section: plan header test-command; per-wave gate-command pytest
message: The Foreman-facing test-command is node scripts/run-all-tests.mjs, while every wave gate is scoped pytest -v on a dated file. The draft never defines what run-all-tests.mjs runs, whether it invokes the conformance harness / zero_inference_lint / table_validator, or which command is authoritative when they disagree. A future maintainer will green the wave pytest and leave the node suite broken (or the reverse), and regressions in dead controls or cost labelling will not be caught at the contract the orchestrator actually runs. Bind one composition rule: run-all-tests.mjs must invoke every wave gate-command plus conformance tools, or drop the node entry and make the pytest root the sole Foreman test-command.

criterion: no silent zero / mislabelled empty; remembered preference and live cadence must stay honest under re-entry
section: Property gates; Hardening-gate obligations; wave deliverables
message: The plan asserts honesty, idempotence, boundedness, and containment as plan-level properties, and says a named property without a matching obligation is a BLOCKER—yet only W1 (escape attempts), W3 (repeat-invocation), and a few numeric bounds are wave-owned. Preference persistence (W19), cadence (W20), inventory ledger writes, and cost migration claim durability-adjacent behaviour without atomic write/lock/concurrency obligations or per-wave idempotence tests. Future maintainers will treat the property-gate section as wallpaper; double-apply preference or cadence ticks will mislabel empty/unknown. Either attach each asserted property to concrete wave ids with named tests, or remove the plan-level assertion so the inclusion test does not lie.

criterion: Cost never fabricates dollars
section: W4 rollup evidence / cost spot-check protocol
message: Dollar honesty rests on a 0-cent independent spot-check and a rule that the aggregation author may not compute the second side. The draft never defines the machine record (fields for author identity, procedure path, session sample set, engine, both totals, disagreement) that the gate validates—only narrative rejection conditions. A future maintainer will store a checkbox “independent: true” and ship fabricated agreement. Specify the spot-check artifact schema, how author identity is host-attested (not agent-self-reported), and the exact gate failure strings when independence or sample floors fail—and refuse PROVEN cost without that artifact.

criterion: unknown ≠ empty ≠ zero
section: Binding definitions (The state trichotomy); W6 NamedState
message: Calling a four-word set a “trichotomy,” then adding a thirteen-state enum plus an allow-list of ok/unmeasured/measurement_failed/timeout/stale/cannot_*, guarantees vocabulary drift the next time someone “adds one more state.” Future maintainers will argue which set is canonical. Rename to “core four (empty / zero_measured / unknown / pending)” plus “extended NamedState registry,” and state that only the registry is renderable—no parallel “trichotomy” brand.

criterion: John can open, run, stop, and restart real Anchor work — including Doctor diagnose and session attach
section: Binding definitions (“end-to-end”); Success criteria; W9–W21; W22
message: Steel-man the plan’s central premise: “we never claim MET until S1; waves only stamp CANDIDATE-MET at rendered-string level; named failure is as good as success for honesty.” That is a strong anti-lying design. It still refutes the North Star’s primary clause. The North Star is a capability claim (“John can … real Anchor work”), not an honesty-on-failure claim. Every surface wave is allowed to go GREEN while the success path is never required: pending, unknown, cannot_*, measurement_failed, or unavailable are all valid “closures.” CANDIDATE-MET therefore means “structure that can fail honestly,” not “John can do the work.” Deferring the only success proof to S1 (W22) after ~21 structural waves makes the failure half of “works end-to-end or fails with a named state” the build’s actual optimization target. Even granted perfect disclosure, the plan can exhaust the build proving it never lies while never proving John can open, run, stop, restart, diagnose, or attach real work. Require at least one forced success-path proof per North-Star verb before that criterion may leave OPEN—mid-build, not only at the S1 cliff—or stop calling structural waves “closing” those criteria.

criterion: John can open, run, stop, and restart real Anchor work
section: Success criteria (Stop summary + restart); W16; W1 task triple; NORTH-STAR CONTROL DECISION (W5)
message: Steel-man: stop is covered because the task triple includes stop-restart, W16 ships an inventory-backed stop summary, and W17 covers restart. That still fails. The North Star lists stop as a peer of open/run/restart. The plan’s success criteria and Phase-3 waves engineer open (W10), run (W10), attach (W11), diagnose (W14–15), restart (W17), and a post-stop summary tile (W16)—not a dead-control contract, cannot-stop reasons, or e2e trace for the Stop control itself. A stop that no-ops, double-fires, or leaves work running can still produce a pretty “nothing in flight / unknown” summary. W5’s control table is said to cover stop, but no surface wave is the forced build-now for Stop the way W10 is for Open/Run. Inventory-backed summary after stop ≠ stop works. Add an explicit Stop control wave (or fold Stop into W16 with the same dead-control + named cannot-stop + e2e obligations as Open/Run), or the stop clause of the North Star has no structural owner.

criterion: unknown ≠ empty ≠ zero (named, user-visible state)
section: Binding definitions (Vocabulary bijection); W8 STATE-VOCABULARY-MAP; Hardening-gate failure-state table vocabulary
message: Steel-man: one machine-read bijection plus table_validator.py makes unknown/empty/zero uncollapsible. The draft then breaks its own premise. Bijection is defined as “every term on both sides appears exactly once.” The hardening row empty-but-valid is required to split into empty, zero_measured, and pending—three surface-native NamedStates from one dependency term. That is a one-to-many map, not a bijection. Either (a) the validator enforces true 1:1 and cannot accept the mandatory split, or (b) “bijection” is prose and the map is many-valued, so “appears exactly once” is false and the gate cannot do what Binding definitions claim. The honesty law this plan exists to kill (merging empty with zero/unknown) sits on that map. Replace “bijection / exactly once” with an explicit, testable relation (e.g. total function from dependency rows to one or more NamedStates, with required coverage of empty and zero_measured as separate surface rows) and make table_validator enforce that relation—or the trichotomy is not machine-enforced as advertised.

criterion: works end-to-end or fails with a named, user-visible state; Steward conversational proof is S1, not a silent claim of this build
section: Binding definitions (“end-to-end”); W9 trace schema; W10–W20 done-whens; W22 S1
message: Steel-man: the plan is unusually careful—proof_level: rendered-string, terminal status refuses unqualified “met,” S1 alone converts CANDIDATE-MET→MET. That protects against silent green. It does not protect the North Star’s “real Anchor work” requirement. W9–W21 define end-to-end as control→handler→capability→generate_html text nodes + node --check + induced faults. No wave requires a live engine session, a real open of real work, a real stop of real work, or a diagnose against a live Doctor reading outside fixtures. So the strongest reading of the plan is: “we will never pretend string-proof is user-proof.” The weakest consequence is also true: the entire structural build can be GREEN with zero evidence that real work ever succeeded. S1 is not a backstop on a mostly-proven system; it is the first and only success trial of the North Star verbs. That is a validation cliff, not progressive proof. Either insert mandatory live-success gates (even narrow ones) for open/run/stop/restart/attach/diagnose before W21 may stamp CANDIDATE-MET, or rewrite success criteria so structural waves may not claim to “close” those criteria at all—only “instrument and fail-honest.”

criterion: without meeting a dead control
section: W3 Capability Inventory; W5 NORTH-STAR CONTROL DECISION; W10 dead_control.py
message: Steel-man: PRESENT requires live probe, transcript, source hash, 14-day bound, and replay-only PRESENT cannot ship a live control—stronger than most inventory schemes. Still insufficient for the North Star. PRESENT answers “is there a bound control / capability on this build?” Dead-control elimination answers “no clickable no-op.” Neither answers “invoking the control performs real work without silent failure.” W10’s contract emits the control whenever inventory is PRESENT and non-STALE; enumerated CannotOpen/CannotRun reasons cover only listed failures. An unlisted failure mode can still yield a live button that misleads (wrong project, half-open session, run handle that never starts)—not a “dead control,” but exactly the user-visible harm the North Star lists alongside dead controls. The freeze path “PRESENT + John’s no further work” can remove build work while leaving only trace/table obligations. Steel-man fails: absence of dead controls ≠ presence of working controls. Tie PRESENT-for-shipping to a success-path probe (or keep the control hidden until a success contract passes), not merely to “handler bound / not canned seed.”

criterion: Every surface that claims health, usage, or diagnose either works end-to-end or fails with a named, user-visible state; Cost never fabricates dollars
section: W4 Rollup Evidence Gate; W12 Usage + time; W13 Cost; Success criteria criterion 3
message: Steel-man: W4 separates NO_AGGREGATOR / READ_FAILED / PROVEN(zero_measured|empty|nonzero); W12/W13 only render through those verdicts and cost_state; dollars never invent from zero. Structurally clean. Consequence: every usage/time rollup may remain NO_AGGREGATOR → perpetual pending, and every cost path unmeasured/measurement_failed, while W12/W13 still done-when and criterion 3 still CANDIDATE-MET. The surfaces “claim” usage/cost by existing as tiles; they only ever show named non-values. That satisfies the failure branch and the anti-fabrication rule, and simultaneously never delivers working usage or cost on v1.2. W12’s Depends-on lists W9 only (not W4); even granting freeze_gate as a cross-cut, nothing requires any rollup to be PROVEN before criterion 3 may candidate-close. For a North Star that names usage as a claimed surface, “all pending forever” is not a closed honesty story—it is an abandoned success story with good labels. Require a minimum PROVEN set (or an explicit signed exit that usage/cost are out of this build with no claiming tiles) before criterion 3 may leave OPEN.

criterion: Every surface that claims health, usage, or diagnose either works end-to-end or fails with a named, user-visible state
section: Success criteria (Doctor); W14 banner_handoff; W15 engines; North Star “health, usage, or diagnose”
message: Steel-man: Doctor diagnose (W14) plus per-engine depth (W15) plus banner→Doctor payload integrity cover “health” because the banner is only an entry point into Doctor. The North Star separately names surfaces that claim health. A health banner that shows green/ok from stale, partial, or one-engine echo while Doctor is honest only after click is still a health-claiming surface that can lie. W14 asserts payload id/hash propagation and bans seed prose in findings; it does not give the banner its own failure-state table, unknown≠empty≠zero (or healthy≠unknown≠degraded) contract, or e2e under induced health-probe faults. Cadence (W20) is status telemetry, not the health claim. Without a first-class honesty contract for the health-claiming chrome itself, the plan steel-mans “diagnose works” while leaving “claims health” unowned.

criterion: Steward conversational proof is a post-build validation session (S1), not a silent claim of this build; John can open, run, stop, and restart…
section: W2 terminal_status; W21 CANDIDATE-MET matrix; W22 S1
message: Steel-man: S1-only MET and BUILD_BLOCKING for the four violation classes correctly implement “not a silent claim of this build.” The premise that this makes the plan safe still fails operationally. W21 may mark criteria 1–10 CANDIDATE-MET after string-level greens; W22 is the first live multi-verb session with John. Any S1 failure reverts criteria to OPEN after the budget for W1–W21 is spent. The plan’s own exit-conjunction and insertion caps manage structural exits, not “we built the wrong thing for 21 waves.” Steel-man of late human validation assumes structural waves reduce S1 risk; under this draft they mostly reduce lying risk. That is valuable and insufficient. Add cheap live checkpoints (even single-verb) after W10 and after Doctor/restart waves, or accept that CANDIDATE-MET rows are not progress markers toward the North Star and must not be reported as such in terminal status.

criterion: stop, and restart … without meeting a dead control; exactly one restart control per restart context (success criteria)
section: W17 RESTART-CONTEXTS.md + restart_control_audit.py
message: Steel-man: written contracts, one entry point per context, HTML audit count==1, preserved/lost tested against the contract—solid for listed contexts. The enumeration is produced in the same wave that audits it (RESTART-CONTEXTS.md is a W17 deliverable). An incomplete list makes the audit pass vacuously: dual competing controls in an unlisted chrome never fail. “Exactly one restart control per restart context” is only as strong as an independent, freeze-time inventory of restart surfaces (W3/W5), not a wave-local list authored beside the code under test. Bind the audit to a W3/W5-frozen context list; treat any rendered restart control whose context id is absent from the freeze as an automatic fail.

criterion: Cost never fabricates dollars
section: W4 cost spot-check; W7 render_cost; W13 cost surfaces
message: Steel-man: 0-cent tolerance, independent second procedure, mid-migration fail-closed to measurement_failed, zero×state matrix, zero_inference_lint—strong against the classic 0⇒subscription bug. Gaps remain. Spot-check is ≥20 sessions / ≥3 per engine over 30 days: agreement on the sample does not constrain unsampled engines, windows, or code paths. W13 removes “every direct dollar-format call site” by aspiration; enforcement is lint + tests in-wave, not a repo-wide forbid on non-render_cost formatters that later waves might add. E2 is banned for dollars, but a measured wrong number that passed a thin spot-check still fabricates dollars. Either widen the gate (all instrumented engines, or continuous reconciliation hook with measurement_failed on drift) or state honestly that the build proves “no zero-inference labelling” and “sample agreement,” not global non-fabrication.

criterion: John can open, run … real Anchor work; works end-to-end …
section: W10 EARLY-SLICE-PARTIAL.md; Binding definitions end-to-end
message: Steel-man: naming W10 as a partial early slice and writing EARLY-SLICE-PARTIAL.md prevents readers from mistaking open/run string-honesty for the full North Star—good. The premise that this slice “engineers the leading clause” still overclaims. After W10 the build has open/run dead-control structure and rendered-string traces, explicitly not a human-driven path and explicitly PARTIAL. The leading North Star clause is not advanced in the North Star’s own sense of “John can … real work”; only the honesty scaffolding for two controls is. Keep the slice, but forbid any status language that open/run criteria are “candidate-closed” solely by W10 unless a live success observation (even a single John-witnessed open+run) is attached. Otherwise the “early value” premise is morale theater.

criterion: usage … works end-to-end or fails with named state; only after rollup evidence gate (success criteria)
section: W12 Depends on; W4; W5 freeze_gate
message: Steel-man: freeze_gate.py blocks all surface waves until inventory+rollup hashes match, so a missing Depends-on edge is cosmetic. Foreman-style orchestration still uses the wave Depends-on graph for scheduling and resume. W12 lists Depends on W9 only, while success criteria say usage/time only after the rollup evidence gate. If freeze_gate is skipped, mis-ordered, or reimplemented incompletely under resume, usage can build against an empty registry. Encode W4 and W5 as hard Depends-on for W12/W13 (and any rollup consumer), not only as a side tool check—duplicate the constraint where the engine actually looks.

criterion: preview that dumps raw binary; File preview human-friendly Office/PDF
section: W18 File preview
message: Steel-man: binary guard + per-format fixtures + no raw signatures in HTML kills the dump-as-text failure mode even if the shared path is imperfect. The deliverable text still says “reusing the working new-window renderer.” If W3 marks preview STUB or the “working” path is environment-specific, W18 may wrap a non-working path and still pass HTML absence-of-bytes tests with shallow stubs. Require the shared path’s PRESENT (or a build-it sub-step) as a gate input to W18, and define “human-friendly” as asserted content shape per format—not only “no PK\x03\x04.”

criterion: Doctor: real diagnose; every surface that claims … diagnose works end-to-end or fails named
section: W14 FAULT-FINDING-CONTRACTS + anti-template test
message: Steel-man: live readings required, seed strings banned, anti-template fault outside the table, payload hash integrity—far better than shell/seed theater. Residual hole: expected finding shape per contracted fault can still be satisfied by shallow “reading quoted, prose generic” diagnostics that look real in tests and fail John in S1. Accept as residual risk or require at least one fault whose correct finding is a structured field assertion (path exists, version matches, count threshold) not only “quotes a reading.”

criterion: without … a preview that dumps raw binary
section: Wave 18 — File preview
message: W18’s “binary guard” is only content-type → named unsupported-preview. There is no path sandbox (resolve under an allowed root; refuse `..`, absolute escape, symlink/junction by name) and no magic-byte / content sniff before render. A path that escapes the intended tree, or a file whose declared type is wrong, can still stream raw bytes into a text view — exactly the North Star violation. The binary-guard test only asserts absence of `PK\x03\x04` on happy-path fixtures; it never forces refusal on path escape or type/magic mismatch. Until escape-attempt + magic-byte refusal are deliverables with acceptance criteria, “no raw binary as text” is unenforced prose.

criterion: Nothing in this effort ships to v1.1.x collaborators
section: Wave 22 — release_guard.py
message: The release guard is specified only as a “branch and channel check.” That does not prove v1.2-only modules (cost_state migration, named_state, dead_control, Doctor engines, new surface handlers) are excluded from v1.1.x packaging, installers, shared artifact channels, or cherry-picks. Collaborators on v1.1.x can still receive this effort’s code/artifacts if packaging is ungoverned. Branch name alone is not “nothing ships.” Require an artifact/package allowlist (or explicit exclude list of this build’s new paths) plus a failing test that a simulated v1.1.x package build cannot include those paths.

criterion: open, run … real Anchor work without a dead control / mislabelled empty; preview that dumps raw binary
section: W1 containment vs W10 / W14 / W18; property gates containment
message: Escape-attempt coverage exists only for Foreman write containment under `planning/sleep-2026-07-28/stage2/`. Open, run workspace resolution, file preview, and Doctor path/version reads have zero escape-attempt acceptance criteria. Property-gate “containment” fires only “where containment is claimed,” and runtime surfaces never claim it — so the gate never fires. A control that opens or previews a path outside the intended workspace can present foreign content as legitimate work, mislabel empty/unknown relative to the wrong root, or dump raw binary. That is a security-shaped honesty failure on the North Star’s open/run/preview verbs, not a nice-to-have hardening add-on. Bind path sandbox + escape refusal into W10 and W18 (and Doctor live path reads in W14) with the same refusal-by-name pattern W1 already uses for build writes.

criterion: Steward conversational proof is a post-build validation session (S1), not a silent claim of this build
section: Wave 2 exit_register; Wave 1 task triple; Wave 5 freeze; Wave 22 S1
message: “Signature validator,” “John’s dated confirmation line,” and freeze/exit stamps are schema fields with no host-bound or out-of-band identity check. `attestation.py` rejects sub-agent EXECUTION-LOG attestations, but nothing equivalent binds John-signed exit rows, the task triple, or the wave-list freeze. A wave or sub-agent can write a plausible confirmation string and green-path exits, freeze, and S1 prerequisites. That reopens silent structural claims of North Star readiness — the exact failure S1 exists to prevent. Specify a non-forgeable confirmation mechanism (host-only prompt, separate signed file John produces outside the agent write path, or equivalent) and a test that agent-written “John” lines are rejected.

criterion: session attach … without … a dead control; fails with a named, user-visible state (unknown ≠ empty)
section: Wave 11 — Session attach honesty
message: Attach honesty covers timeout vs unknown_session, single error print, and Retry/cannot-retry. It never binds the attach request to a verified session identity (stable session id, process handle, owner, generation token). A wrong-session attach that returns success with another session’s stream is neither timeout nor unknown — it is a silent wrong attach, which is a security and honesty failure under “session attach” in the North Star. Add a cannot-attach / identity-mismatch named state, require handle verification before success, and an induced-fault test where a mismatched id cannot render as a successful attach.

criterion: Doctor diagnose … every surface that claims health … or diagnose either works end-to-end or fails with a named, user-visible state
section: Wave 14 — Doctor diagnose
message: W14 bans fixed seed strings and requires findings to quote live readings (paths, versions, counts). It has no redaction or refusal path when a live reading contains credentials, tokens, or API keys. A diagnose that “works” by painting secrets into the Doctor tile is a confident wrong health/diagnose surface — parallel to raw-binary preview on the file surface. Require a secret-pattern refusal (or redacted-reading named state) with a test that injects a key-shaped reading and asserts it never appears in rendered HTML, and that the surface shows a named cannot_show_reading / redacted state instead of success-with-secret.

criterion: unknown ≠ empty ≠ zero; surfaces fail with named states rather than silent wrong answers
section: Wave 9 — fault_inject.py
message: `fault_inject.py` can induce timeout, missing capability, empty result, unmeasured cost, and stale telemetry. No deliverable requires test-only enforcement (import guard, env flag, refuse outside pytest/CI). If production handlers can call it, live surfaces can be forced into fabricated named states — honesty inverted. Add a hard production refuse path and a test that production-mode import/invoke raises and cannot alter rendered state.

criterion: Nothing in this effort ships to v1.1.x collaborators
section: Wave 3 — artifacts/transcripts/; Wave 22 release_guard
message: Capability probes capture live transcripts under the shared planning tree, replayed many times, with a 14-day staleness rule on verdicts but no redaction, retention bound, or scrub gate on transcript bodies. Live v1.2 environment output (paths, session ids, cost rows, engine errors) can land in repo-tracked artifacts that collaborators receive. Release_guard’s branch/channel check does not scrub or quarantine these. Require secret scrub + explicit non-shipping classification for `artifacts/transcripts/` (or store outside the collaborator-facing tree) with a release-guard test that fails if raw transcript material is present in a v1.1.x-publishable package set.

criterion: open, run … real Anchor work without meeting a dead control
section: Wave 10 — open_work / run_work
message: Run enumerates CannotRun reasons (no target, engine unavailable, prior run in flight, capability absent) but never constrains how project/target strings reach the engine process. Unsanitized argv/shell construction lets a crafted project path or target name become command injection — a successful-looking Run that is not “real Anchor work.” That is a security-shaped dead/wrong control. Enumerate injection/escape as CannotRun (or refuse) reasons, ban shell=True-style invocation in acceptance tests, and add a fixture that dangerous metacharacters in a target cannot spawn unintended commands and must render a named cannot-run state.

criterion: preview that dumps raw binary; open … real Anchor work
section: Wave 18 — download affordance
message: Unsupported types get “named unsupported-preview + download affordance,” but download is not bound to the same path sandbox as preview. A download that follows an escaped path exfiltrates arbitrary files while the UI claims a safe named state. Extend the W18 path sandbox to the download action with an escape-attempt test; otherwise the named state is honesty theater around a second exfil channel.
